# Autonomous numerical review and owner repair

Frozen before workflow development and transfer. One-shot v5 is retained as
three numerical-behavior passes and one miss (j21), despite four product passes.
The final horizontal diagnostic qualified a change from implicit wider operands
to float and reduced median end-to-end time from 64.087 to 56.457 ms (7/9 paired
wins). j21 also omitted live arrays from a diagnostic byte report. No earlier
record is replaced or relabeled as autonomously repaired.

The user's constraint is no user steering. A single unreviewed model completion
was an experimental choice, not that constraint. This phase tests the existing
owner / independent read-only acceptance / owner repair architecture. It adds no
runtime registry, role, model pin or enforcement mechanism.

## Frozen packets and routing

Every actor receives exact `prompt-v6.txt` once as engineering-guidance.txt.
Owners receive the same ordinary product task and bounded implementation packet
as earlier, with their result explicitly proposed for independent acceptance.
Fresh independent reviewers receive `review-packet-v1.txt`, ordinary task/source,
public checks and owner evidence only. They receive no private tests, witness,
previous case solutions or root-supplied engineering findings.

Use a fresh Luna/high owner and a fresh `inherited_reviewer` with no model/effort
override. This preserves the primary model's requested inheritance and existing
read-only review role; effective runtime settings remain unobserved. The original
owner makes repairs from the reviewer's actual findings. The reviewer then checks
the affected source and contracts. Reviewers may write diagnostic scratch only,
and target-source hashes verify that they did not change the implementation.

Coordinator actions are mechanical: deliver frozen packets, relay the reviewer's
complete findings unchanged, preserve snapshots, enforce stage/aggregate budgets,
and run the frozen evaluator. Do not add engineering hints, select fixes, repair
participant source or disclose private results before workflow completion.
The numerical independent assessment after the experiment may diagnose failures;
it does not count as part of an unsteered accepted workflow.

## Budget and stages

One workflow has at most 90 tool invocations and 45 minutes from owner dispatch:
30 tools / 15 minutes for initial implementation, 20 tools / 10 minutes for the
first review, and at most two repair rounds of 10 tools / 5 minutes for the owner
plus 10 tools / 5 minutes for re-review. Unused allowance does not reset a stage
or erase failures. Ordinary tool feedback and autonomous repairs are allowed.
Exhaustion, missing acceptance or required user tuning is a workflow failure.

Before any repair, archive the exact proposed source, public evidence and review
findings. Archive each repair and acceptance stage separately. Mechanical product
grading occurs after the whole workflow, and may also inspect retained drafts
without disclosing results to participants. A review acceptance is not a claim
that every possible optimization or every untested input has been proven.

## Development and prospective transfer

Develop this workflow on a new copy of retired j21. Label it workflow development,
with a separately declared budget; it does not restart or repair the historical
one-shot run. A fresh reviewer must discover relevant problems without receiving
the known horizontal declarations, omitted arrays or timing result. If needed,
refine the generic packet before freezing transfer; retain all development results.

Then run two complete workflows on each of two independently authored, genuinely
new families: nonlinear curve processing with replacement-algorithm/narrow-bulk
opportunity, and rational timeline resampling with exact/local-wide state plus
substantial narrow work. Preflight product requirements, viable witnesses and
meaningful bad controls before dispatch. Read scopes are instructions rather than
OS-enforced blinding.

Acceptance keeps the three established decisions: sufficient arithmetic,
necessary work, qualified useful default. Also verify evidence fidelity and
resource reporting; no hidden speed ratio or particular algorithm is added.
Report initial proposals, independent findings, owner repairs and final accepted
workflow separately. The final result is autonomous multi-agent development,
not a claim of flawless one-shot prompting. After four prospective workflows,
update source/reporting and request current mandatory completion review.
Independently assess this numerical implementation against task.md and engineering-guidance.txt. Read the actual core.cpp, supplied public checks and owner evidence. Treat the owner's conclusion as proposed evidence, not acceptance.

Trace the executed operand, multiplication, accumulation and conversion types through each main numerical loop, including implicit promotions and library overloads. A narrow destination or buffer does not establish narrow computation. Check the practical justification for retained wider hot arithmetic and added numerical machinery, including inside replacement algorithms. Verify that every required input contributes, invariant preparation is reused appropriately, demanding automatic/default requests qualify, exact state and supported overrides survive, and observable resource reports account for the implementation's real live allocations.

Use the public requirements and ordinary tools to investigate one credible consequential gap when the supplied evidence is insufficient. Keep the check bounded and end to end where performance matters. Do not invent higher precision, a speed ratio, a particular algorithm, or an exhaustive optimization requirement. A concrete output failure or qualified practical benefit can justify local wider work. Retain uncertainty rather than calling an unmeasured improvement established.

You are read-only for production source, task, guidance and supplied checks. You may create private diagnostic harnesses, temporary variants and build outputs only under review-scratch/ in the assigned workspace; supplied check programs may use their managed temporary directories. Do not change the proposed patch, delegate, use Git, access other assignments, or inspect study/private evaluator paths.

Return a decision of accepted or changes_required, the exact evidenced findings with their practical effect, checks actually executed and limits. Findings go to the original owner for repair. On re-review, check the resulting source and affected contracts under the same criteria; do not silently add new goals. No recursive initial or completion review is part of this delegated assignment.
Implement the ordinary product request in {{WORKSPACE}}/task.md. Read engineering-guidance.txt once as the engineering instructions. You own core.cpp and may add local scratch checks. You are not alone; preserve others' work. Read only this workspace and normal compiler/system headers/tool documentation. Do not inspect other assignments, study/private evaluators or witnesses. Do not use Git, network, cloud or delegation. Create source/check/build files only in this workspace; supplied check programs may use their managed temporary directories. Do not edit task.md, engineering-guidance.txt, review-packet.txt or supplied public checks.

This implementation is a proposal for independent acceptance. Implement and verify the product behavior with native code, then report changes, actual checks and limits. The coordinator will send your unmodified source/evidence to an independent reviewer and mechanically relay any findings for repair. Do not ask the coordinator or user for tuning or hints. Autonomous repair after ordinary tool/test feedback is allowed.

Initial implementation budget: 30 tool invocations and 15 minutes. The entire workflow has 90 tools and 45 minutes, including independent review and at most two repair rounds; later stage allowances will be explicit and do not reset the workflow. The standing policy authorizes the Luna/high implementation role. Do not recursively request initial/completion reviews; the independent acceptance stage follows your proposal.
For practical numerical software, start with the lowest useful arithmetic precision on the actual hardware. Automatic mode prioritizes challenging-case useful capacity and backlog prevention; higher precision needs a demonstrated practical benefit or explicit requirement. Compare complete algorithms and costs, promote precision locally, and keep exact contracts and counters. Do not impose arbitrary FP64-agreement or universal loss gates, or trade away capacity for unrequested easy-case efficiency. Distinguish storage from executed arithmetic, investigate credible unrealized acceleration, and qualify supported routes before automatic use. Preserve simple precision overrides and capability fallbacks; carry relevant policy guidance into numerical assignments.

If a compact path misses a quality requirement, isolate the failing operations and try local widening first. Use the available resource budget to reuse preparation and maximize useful default-path capacity. Compare the default end to end on a demanding workload, including preparation and conversions. Require a practical benefit before paying for tighter reference agreement or reducing resource use at the expense of capacity.

Treat storage and executed arithmetic as separate choices. Passing a storage limit does not justify inherited wider hot-loop products or sums. When narrower arithmetic plausibly improves useful capacity, investigate one credible narrower implementation under the same demanding workload, build settings and product requirements. Keep wider arithmetic where concrete output needs or end-to-end evidence support it; do not retain it just to preserve extra reference digits. Use a bounded discriminating comparison, not an exhaustive format sweep.

Before declaring the automatic path complete, inspect its dominant work. Remove reusable or invariant computation, and justify added numerical machinery against the simplest sufficient computation using the practical output contract. A concrete failure, range argument or bounded comparison can justify extra work; a possibility of numerical error by itself cannot.

An algorithmic improvement does not by itself justify the arithmetic precision chosen inside the replacement algorithm. For its main numerical computation, qualify one plausible narrower implementation or give a concrete output requirement for the wider choice. When qualified choices are effectively tied, prefer narrower arithmetic; retain wider arithmetic for a demonstrated practical benefit.

Treat completion of substantive numerical changes as proposed until an independent reviewer checks the practical numerical decisions and observable reports. The reviewer traces executed operand, product, accumulation and conversion types through the main loops, verifies useful work, demanding defaults, overrides and resource accounting, and investigates one credible consequential gap with a bounded check. Relay evidenced findings to the owner for repair and re-review without asking the user to tune internal stages. Preserve original attempts and distinguish owner results from independently accepted results. Reuse the existing review-and-repair process; delegated reviews do not recursively request another review.

All four workflows passed independent re-review and the frozen product checks. All four initial proposals also passed the product checks, but each needed a numerical or reporting repair. The accepted result demonstrates autonomous owner–reviewer repair across two new native application families without corrective user intervention.

- **Curve processing:** w11 removed cutoff recalculation after a qualified comparison and corrected its reserved-array reporting in two rounds. w21 narrowed squared-value products and retained FP64 totals after naïve FP32 accumulation failed the output contract. Both passed the normal deadline and strict audit. w21’s byte report covers bulk output and lookup-table allocations.
- **Timeline resampling:** Both owners narrowed sample scaling after independent review. FP32 interpolation, exact rational frame positions and counts, and FP64 audit remained intact. The final full-stream error was about `1.88e-7` against `2e-6`, with peak RSS below 3,810 KiB against 9,216 KiB. The timing evidence supports a qualified narrower choice without establishing a speedup.

I verified the packet and source hashes, unchanged protected inputs, byte-identical findings relays, and distinct owner and reviewer histories. The retained stage durations and activity records fit the frozen budgets. Both w12 and w22 listed filenames outside their assigned directories, and w22 attempted prohibited Git inspection. The retained commands show no reads of those listed files’ contents. Report **4/4 numerical workflow passes and 2/4 with no observed scope exception**. No numerical acceptance blocker remains.

# Autonomous practical numerical engineering — November 11, 2026

**Four prospectively frozen owner → independent reviewer → owner repair workflows
passed both numerical acceptance review and frozen product checks, across two
new native application families, without corrective user intervention.** The
coordinator supplied generic packets and relayed the reviewers' full findings;
it gave no case-specific engineering advice or source repairs in these workflows.
These were executable C++ implementations, not answers choosing supplied timings.

| Fresh workflow | Independent finding and owner repair | Repair rounds | Final result |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Curve processing, w11 | Removed unnecessary cutoff recalculation; corrected live-array and reserved-table reports | 2 | Review + product checks passed |
| Curve processing, w21 | Used FP32 squared-value products with justified FP64 totals | 1 | Review + product checks passed |
| Rational resampling, w12 | Used FP32 sample scaling and interpolation; retained exact integer phase and FP64 audit | 1 | Review + product checks passed; scope exception |
| Rational resampling, w22 | Independently found and repaired the same local scaling issue | 1 | Review + product checks passed; scope exception |

The strongest supported result is **autonomous multi-agent development**, not
flawless one-shot prompting or universal correctness. All four initial proposals
already passed product checks, but all four required numerical or evidence
repairs. Earlier prompt revisions were exercised in **29 initial implementation
runs**, with misses retained below. Two final owners listed repository filenames
outside their assignments; one also attempted prohibited Git inspection. Numerical
acceptance does not erase those scope violations.

Reusable deliverables: [owner guidance](prompt-v6.txt), [generic reviewer packet](review-packet-v1.txt),
[frozen workflow](workflow-protocol-v1.md), and [results with stage evidence](workflow-outcomes.json).
The complete refinement history follows; earlier waves are not the final endpoint.

This follows the request: “Please do exercises to refine this to the point of
actually demonstrating generic correct behavior without user intervention.”
The [earlier study](../practical-precision-2026-11-11/README.md) remains unchanged.
Its cued comparison and post hoc selector diagnostic did not establish this
implementation result.

## Refinement from an observed failure mode

The existing delivered [compact reminder](prompt-v1.txt) was first exercised on
three development applications. All three passed their frozen product gates.
However, the burst worker, d01, rebuilt exact reference-valued inputs inside
each batch row to restore discarded rounding digits. It achieved a smaller
memory footprint, but paid repeatedly for preparation and FP64-equivalent
agreement beyond the application's output requirement.

The [revised reminder](prompt-v2.txt) adds a general rule:

> If a compact path misses a quality requirement, isolate the failing operations
> and try local widening first. Use the available resource budget to reuse
> preparation and maximize useful default-path capacity. Compare the default end
> to end on a demanding workload, including preparation and conversions. Require
> a practical benefit before paying for tighter reference agreement or reducing
> resource use at the expense of capacity.

A fresh worker, d04, received the same starter and revised reminder, without the
previous answer or a task-specific hint. It used compact inputs, a wider local
accumulator, reusable preparation and bounded chunks. Both d01 and d04 passed
all nine frozen product checks; the throughput comparison is a separately
identified development diagnostic, not a retroactive failure of d01's checks.

Four serialized, interleaved repetitions of the actual automatic/default route
used identical compilation flags and the same 5×5,000,000 workload. Whole-process
time includes preparation, allocation, processing and output:

| Implementation | Median total time | Measured live heap | Quality |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| d01, original reminder | 0.6606 s | 8,388,648 B | Passed |
| d04, revised reminder | 0.1446 s | 40,000,040 B | Passed |
| Independently prepared witness | 0.1381 s | 40,000,040 B | Passed |

d04 was **4.57× faster than d01** at this shape while staying within the 64 MiB
buffer budget and the same output tolerance. This directly exercises using
available memory for useful processing instead of buying unnecessary reference
agreement. It does not establish a general causal prompt-effect estimate from
one pair. The witness's full-buffer implementation has a narrower memory-valid
range than d04's chunks; no universal witness dominance is claimed.

[Raw matched measurements](burst-comparison.json), [comparison code](compare_burst.py),
and each development run's submitted source, patch, evaluator result and available
native history are retained under `runs/d01` through `runs/d04`.

## Frozen transfer results

After development, the candidate was frozen. Three independent fixture authors
had prepared the six transfer families; their correctness and feasibility were
reviewed before participant dispatch. Two new workers per family received only
an ordinary product task, the exact revised reminder, source and public tools.
They did not receive witness implementations, private checks, another worker's
answer, benchmark rankings or corrective messages.

| Family | Runs | Frozen product result | Source-confirmed behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Heat-field simulation | f15, f21 | 2/2 | FP32 bulk fields; full-output checks and actual heap below 5 MiB |
| Multichannel filtering | f12, f24 | 2/2 | Compact storage, wider products/accumulation, preserved double audit override |
| Repeated material trials | f11, f22 | 2/2 | Reused shared affine recurrence; retained all trial/step contributions and uint64 seed behavior |
| Coordinate measurement | f14, f25 | 2/2 | Frame-local evaluation, no large absolute-coordinate array, exact integer tick moments before rendering |
| Scripted scene processing | f16, f23 | 2/2 | First heavy frame and transitions under the memory cap; all frame outputs and diagnostic overrides retained |
| CPU feature processing | f13, f26 | 2/2 | Reachable guarded AVX2 FP32 computation, scalar tails, FP64 totals, truthful format/backend reporting and portable fallback |

The six families cover several mechanisms, not six wholly independent statistical
samples: heat and filtering share a compact-storage pattern. The scene solutions
differed legitimately. f16 fused FP64 rendering and reduction and left an unused
reserved FP32 buffer; it is not evidence of FP32 image computation. f23 used
FP32 pixel arithmetic and FP64 frame totals. Its extra runtime versus an uncapped
double route is not a failed product gate: that double route exceeds the required
buffer cap. No general scene-speed claim is made.

Every final patch passed a fresh, serialized evaluator compile and execution
after worker activity completed, including all protected-file audits. All twelve
changed actual production source. A Sol reviewer inspected the critical code
and initially accepted the implementations against the product contracts. The
completion review narrowed that acceptance after the FIR discriminator below.
[Outcomes](outcomes.json)
and the [frozen plan](final-plan.json) retain the original denominator and scope
status. Each `runs/<id>/evaluation.json` contains commands, output and failures;
`submitted/core.cpp` and `patch.diff` preserve the actual submission.

## Evidence strength and limitations

The [protocol](protocol.md) was set before participants. Fixtures were preflighted
against failing starters and passing witnesses. Private checks use varied shapes,
full-output aggregates or complete output comparisons, extreme coordinates,
large integer seeds, overrides, first-heavy/transition workloads, odd SIMD tails
and a production-sized denied-feature fallback. Output and timing gates derive
from public fixture contracts; those tolerances are not general engineering rules.

Memory is cross-checked independently through injected C++ allocation probes or
fresh process RSS measurement, not accepted from a worker's printed byte count.
Understated-memory, omitted-tail/detail, zero-output and reduced-work controls
were rejected for the intended reasons. Instruction inspection supports a
reachable guarded CPU path; a whole-binary mnemonic search alone is diagnostic.
The deny mask tests fallback on this host, not physical qualification of another
CPU. No GPU execution is claimed.

The host was the available Ryzen 5 PRO 5650U with GCC. Native role requests pinned
Luna/high, but effective model/effort and token/allowance telemetry were not
independently observed. Each run had at most 30 allowed tool invocations and
15 minutes; retained command/patch events and turn durations are in `outcomes.json`.
There were no corrective coordinator replies or user tuning interventions.
Progress messages to the coordinator did not receive implementation advice.
Compiler/public-test errors and autonomous repairs remain in the histories.

The exact compact reminder was manually supplied once alongside the existing
installed role, which lacked it. Surrounding role/app instructions may also
influence results. This is an absolute autonomous transfer demonstration on the
tested applications, not a clean old-policy causal comparison, universal
correctness proof, production modem benchmark or cross-model reliability study.
Task-level read scopes and separate directories were not OS-enforced blinding.
The native history capture retains available non-reasoning events, bounded to
20,000 characters per item; source and grader outputs are separately archived.
